title: Ribbon with a play
idea: Shelf's bookmark hangs from the top edge of the tile like the ribbon marker in a hardback, so the tile becomes the book and only the ribbon's body and notched tail show. A play is cut out of the body: kept for later, and ready to listen to.
built: Ribbon 40 dp wide (the solid reference's width), running from y 0 so it passes the top of every mask and the launcher's parallax, down to tips at y 79, with Shelf's notch (11/34 of the width, 12.9 dp) and tips r 1.76; the rounded tips reach 30.2 dp from the centre. The play's slanted edges are parallel to the notch's (tan 11/17), which makes it 24 dp tall and 18.5 deep, a little slimmer than equilateral; its two back corners then share the tips' 57 degrees, and the band of paper under it runs parallel to the notch. Corners r 1.76, like the tips. It sits 0.35 of the way from box centring to centroid centring, and its height is set by the 10.5 dp band under it, which puts its centre at y 46.9: walls 11.8 left, 11.1 right (to the rounded tip) and 10.5 under, measured square to the notch.
small: The cuts keep a lip of tile above the ribbon, 3 px at 48, 2 at 32 and 1 at 16, the smallest detail each size allows: bled to the edge, the paper merged with light browser toolbars and the tile read as a dark U. The ribbon's square top corners still say it comes from under the edge, and every cut keeps the play's rhyme with the notch. 48: ribbon 28 px, notch 9 px over a 14 px half width (Shelf's slope), play 17 px with its flat side on column 18; walls 8, 6.8 and 6.6 px. 32: ribbon 18 px, notch 6 px, play 12 px on column 12, a little larger than the master's so it holds on a 2x toolbar. 16: ribbon 8 px, notch 4 px at 45 degrees as in small.svg, play a 3 x 5 pixel staircase whose 45-degree steps match the notch, with its centroid on the centre line. Glyph: there is no tile to hang from, so it is the whole bookmark with its round shoulders, 16 px wide, with a 10 px play on column 8.
risks: A bookmark with a play in it is close to Google Play Books. One colour, a modest hole and the ribbon running off the tile keep some distance, but this is the main risk. The bleed relies on the tile's edge being visible: on a wallpaper near graphite the ribbon's top reads as the bookmark's own, flat in the squircle and arched in the circle and teardrop; on a pale wallpaper the paper merges with the background, and the tile becomes a dark frame round a bookmark-shaped opening with the play floating in it, which still reads. The toolbar cuts need a lip of tile for the same reason, so they show the ribbon starting just under the edge. The launch screens and the website need an edge for the ribbon to hang from, such as the top of the screen; Android 12's circle-masked splash would cut it with the circle.
